question: Can a mixture of a softmax RNN and a pointer over recent context, gated by a sentinel, predict rare and unseen words better than a plain softmax LSTM, and what benchmark can test long-range context?
hypothesis: The pointer component lets the model reproduce rare words and frees RNN hidden-state capacity, so it should beat an LSTM, most on rare words.
contributions: State-of-the-art Penn Treebank perplexity (70.9) with far fewer parameters than a standard softmax LSTM

method.summary: A pointer sentinel-LSTM adds a pointer-sum attention over the last L=100 hidden states; a sentinel element in the attention softmax gives the gate g that routes mass to the vocabulary softmax. Trained on PTB and WikiText-2 following Zaremba/Gal setups with longer BPTT.

models.name: Gal (2015) Variational LSTM medium/large

training.objective: cross-entropy of the mixture; pointer loss -log(g + sum_{i in I(y,x)} a_i)
training.lr_schedule: halve learning rate when validation perplexity is worse than previous iteration
training.epochs: stop when validation perplexity fails to improve for three epochs or at 64 epochs
training.dropout: 0.5 variational dropout on input to each RNN layer and on final RNN output; zoneout on recurrent connections
training.regularisation: zoneout and variational dropout; gradient rescale when global norm exceeds 1
training.hardware: 12GB K80 GPU mentioned (Gal large OOM on WikiText-2)

other.bptt: k1=1, k2=L: backprop L steps every timestep; only final word's loss used
other.stale_outputs: window of RNN outputs regenerated after each gradient update

terms.definition: A sentinel value is inserted at the end of a search space ... Our sentinel value terminates the pointer search space and distributes the rest of the probability mass to the RNN vocabulary.
probability mass of a word is the sum of attention over all positions where it appears

lineage.note: pointer attention over input; cannot output words outside input
